label: Astromaterial
definition: Any material that meets one of the following conditions: 1) Recovered from space, 2) Extraterrestrial in origin, 3) Paragenetically linked to a material that meets condition 1 or 2 or occurs as a direct product of some process involving an astromaterial.

label: Collection Object
definition: A physical object that belongs to a museum collection.

label: Compound Specimen
definition: A collection object comprised of one or more discernible parts, called constituent parts, unified by physical attachment. The object's identity is determined by its constituent parts, which are distinguished from one another within a specific context.

label: Compound Specimen Model
definition: A conceptual data model in which a single physical object, a compound specimen, is composed of and defined by its constituent parts.

label: Constituent Part
definition: Physically discernible and proximal parts of a compound specimen identified by a single determination based on physical and chemical exclusivity relative to the parent specimen.
usage_note: A constituent part belongs to one and only one constituent part type and defined in terms of role and proportion relative to the parent compound specimen.

label: Constituent Part Proportion
definition: Refers to the qualitative or quantitative representation of the abundance of a Constituent Part within a parent Compound Specimen.

label: Constituent Part Relation
definition: A described uni-directional association between two constituent parts, a source and target, within the scope of the parent compound specimen. A relation is defined from the perspective of the source constituent part and described using a relation predicate.
usage_note: One constituent part may be associated with multiple constituent part relations in either role. Each constituent part relation only exists between the two member constituent parts.

label: Constituent Part Relation Type
definition: A term from a controlled vocabulary to describe the constituent part relation

label: Constituent Part Role
definition: Specifies the relationship between a Constituent Part and its parent compound specimen. Roles are dependent upon both the part and parent object. For instance, a rock (constituent part type) within the parent specimen plays the role of clast and is dependent on both the constituent part and the parent specimen for its existence.

label: Continuent
definition: A continuant is an entity that persists, endures, or continues to exist through time while maintaining its identity. Continuants can preserve their identity even while gaining and losing material parts.

label: Determination
definition: The identity of a specimen represented by a name based on formal criteria evaluated by a domain expert. In biological collections, the determination is represented by a taxonomic classification, primarily a genus and species (e.g., Vulpes vulpes, Accipiter cooperii). In the geosciences domain, examples of determination include Almandine, Granite, and Plantae.

label: Fossil
definition: Any remains, trace, or imprint of a plant or animal preserved in the Earth's crust since some past geologic or prehistoric time; loosely, any evidence of past life.

label: Geologic Material
definition: An amount of matter primarily (dominantly) having parts created by geologic processes and can include minor parts that are not of geologic origin, such as organic material, and can be solid, fluid, or a mix

label: Geologic Material Relation
definition: A perceived association between two geologic materials described by a relation predicate.

label: Geologic Object
definition: An amount of matter primarily having parts created by geologic processes and composed of one or more Constituent Parts unified by physical attachment. Geologic Objects may include minor parts not of geologic origin, such as organic material or synthetic material generated as a close approximation.
source: Garcia et al. (2019) and Brodaric & Richard (2021)

label: Geological Specimen
definition: A collection object comprised in part of geologic material

label: Material Entity
definition: An entity that exists in full during the length of time of its existence, persists through this time while maintaining its identity and has no temporal parts.

label: Mineral
definition: A naturally occurring element or chemical compound that is normally crystalline and formed due to geological processes

label: Mineraloid
definition: An amount of amorphous material; commonly the product of rapid cooling of melted material. Includes natural glasses in Earth and extraterrestrial material, some biogenic mineral products, and anthromophomorphic manufactured material.

label: Museum Collection
definition: An object aggregate that has as member parts a material sample that is located in a museum as a result of a process of curation.

label: Object
definition: An object is a maximal causally unified material entity, meaning b is a material entity which is such that its material parts are tied together in such a way that, in environments typical for entities of the type in question

label: Object Aggregate
definition: A material entity consisting exactly of a plurality of objects as continuant (member) parts at all times at which the object aggregate exists.

label: Physical Collection
definition: Designates an aggregated group of tangible objects with a focal characteristic assembled and maintained by an individual or organization over time. A collection comprises multiple items that are conceptually or physically arranged together for a specific purpose and audience, according to a collection plan

label: Physical Object
definition: Items of a material nature that are units for documentation and have physical boundaries that separate them completely in an objective way from other objects.

label: Relation Predicate
definition: The term describing the nature of the relationship between two constituent parts within the scope of a compound specimen

label: Rock
definition: A consolidated or unconsolidated aggregate of mineral grains consisting of one or more mineral species and having some degree of chemical and mineralogic constancy

label: Simple Specimen
definition: A collection object identified by a single determination without discernible parts.

label: Simple Specimen Model
definition: The conceptual model for the digital representation of physical specimens where each entity is  characterized by one and only one determination without any discrenible parts.

label: Source Role
definition: A term describing the role played by the source constituent part in a constituent part relation

label: Target Role
definition: A term describing the role played by the target constituent part in a constituent part relation

label: Unconsolidated
definition: Unconsolidated earth material is an 'earth material' that is constituted by an aggregate of solid particles but is not consolidated into a 'rock' it self.

label: Constituent Part Type
definition: A value belonging to a top-level, generalized categorization scheme for constituent parts where each constituent part belongs to and only one constituent part type. For any given collection, these constituent part types should comprehensively account for all parts found across every specimen in that collection.

label: Geochronologic Boundary
definition: Temporal boundaries defined with reference to some geologic evidence such as, for instance, fossil appearance/disappearance or significant change in local rock lithology.

label: Geochronologic Interpretation
definition: An interpretation made by a geologist of the age of a specimen made by statistical analysis of a single collection of observations. A specimen may have multiple geochronological interpretations made on it, each related to a different observation collection.

label: Geochronologic Unit
definition: A specialized time ordinal interval used to subdivide geologic time based on a corresponding chronostratigraphic unit.

label: Geochronology
definition: The science of determining absolute ages of geological events and Earth materials. The primary technique utilizes radioactive isotopes and the production and accumulation of radiogenic daughter isotopes naturally present on Earth. It can be applied to various samples, including rocks, minerals, and biological materials.

label: Geologic Event
definition: An identifiable event during which one or more geologic processes act to modify geologic entities.

label: Geologic Process
definition: A natural process that affects the geologic record by acting upon one geologic entity to produce another geologic entity at a later time.
source: Neuendorf et al. (2005), Richard et al. (2007)

label: Geologic Timescale
definition: A temporal reference system that subdivides all the time since Earth formed into named intervals (units) of abstract time and subdivides all the rocks formed since Earth formed into the successions of rock formed during each particular interval of time

label: Half-life
definition: The length of time over which half the atoms of radioactive isotopes decay. The half-life remains constant as the number of atoms is reduced, resulting in an exponential rate of decay

label: Interpreted Age
definition: The age of a geologic event that resulted in the formation of a geologic material that is expressed numerically and based on the results of a dating technique such as radiometric dating or dendrochronology.

label: Lower Temporal Boundary
definition: The maximum limit or latest point in time allowed for a specific event, process, or condition to occur or be considered within a given context or timescale.
usage_note: Equivalent to time:startTime and oldest age

label: Radioactive Decay
definition: The process where an unstable parent isotope loses particles from its atomic nucleus (decay) to form a daughter isotope (product) at a constant rate

label: Radiometric Age
definition: Geologic age expressed in years determined by quantitatively measuring radioactive elements and their decay products

label: Radiometric Dating
definition: Proper chronological placement of a feature, object, or happening in the geologic time scale without reference to its absolute age.

label: Regional Timescale
definition: A family of geologic timescales based on the strata and fossil record observed in a specific area, typically at the country or regional level.

label: Relative Age
definition: The geologic age of a fossil organism, rock, or geologic feature or event defined relative to other organisms, rocks, or features or events rather than in terms of years.

label: Relative Dating
definition: Proper chronological placement of a feature, object, or happening in the geologic time scale without reference to its absolute age.

label: Temporal Coordinate System
definition: A temporal system where time positions are measurements expressed numerically on a scale

label: Temporal Ordinal Reference System
definition: An ordered system of named intervals
usage_note: Each interval belongs to a rank in a mono-hierarchical structure where each parent is divided into one or many children of the next finer rank. This structure allows the set of temporal positions are uniquely ordered relative to the reference system.

label: Time Interval
definition: A temporal entity with an extent or duration

label: Time Ordinal Interval
definition: A named or identified interval from a temporal ordinal reference system

label: Upper Temporal Boundary
definition: The lower limit or earliest point in time allowed for a specific event, process, or condition to occur or be considered within a given context or timescale.
usage_note: Equivalent to time:endTime and youngest age

label: Geologic Environment
definition: Physical conditions found on the Earth's surface, which are determined by factors such as climate, tectonics, physiography, geography and within the Earth's interior, determined by pressure, temperature, chemical environment, and tectonics.

label: Geologic Event Environment
definition: The physical setting within which a Geologic Event takes place.

label: Geologic Feature
definition: A physical or conceptual feature that is hypothesized to exist coherently in the Earth and that results from geological processes.

label: Geologic Structure
definition: A pattern in a rock body (foliation, fold) or a feature occurring between rock bodies (contact, fracture).

label: Petrographic Province
definition: A broad area in which similar igneous rocks are formed during the same period of igneous activity.

label: Physiographic Province
definition: A region in which all parts are similar in geologic structure and climate and which has consequently had a unified geomorphic history; a region whose pattern of relief features or landforms differs significantly from adjacent regions

label: Province
definition: Any large area or region considered as a whole, all parts characterized by similar features or a history differing significantly from adjacent areas.

label: Quarry
definition: An open or surface mineral working, usually for extracting building stone, such as slate, limestone, etc. It is distinguished from a mine because a quarry usually is open at the top and front, and, in ordinary use of the term, by the character of the material extracted.

label: Tectonic Province
definition: Groups of provinces linked by a common tectonic history are designated tectonic provinces. Tectonic provinces may contain a collection of sedimentary, igneous, structural, metamorphic, and metallogenic provinces.

label: Tectonic Setting
definition: A geologic event environment defined by relationships to tectonic plates on or in the Earth.

label: Terrane
definition: A fault-bounded area or region with different layers, rock structures, and geologic history from nearby areas that are not connected to them by unconformable contacts or changes in the rock's surface.

label: Mine
definition: A work for excavating minerals using pits, shafts, levels, tunnels, etc., as opposed to a quarry, where the whole excavation is open. In general, the existence of a mine is determined by the mode in which the mineral is obtained, not by its chemical or geological character. The term also includes only excavations for their minerals or valuable mineral deposits.

label: Concept
definition: Unit of knowledge created by a unique combination of characteristics

label: Conceptual Model
definition: An abstract model or representation of data for a particular domain or field of study, independent of any specific software or information system.

label: Data Model
definition: Graphical and/or lexical representation of data, specifying their properties, structure, and interrelationships

label: Logical Data Model
definition: A data model that includes all entities and the relationships among them based on the structures identified in a conceptual data model and that specifies all attributes for each entity.

label: Model
definition: A simplified representation or abstraction of a system, process, or concept

label: Ontology
definition: Specification of concrete or abstract things, and the relationships among them, in a prescribed domain of knowledge

label: Physical Data Model
definition: A technical representation detailing how data is physically organized and constrained within a database system, focusing on tables, columns, and constraints rather than entities and attributes.
source: Agile Data Warehousing for the Enterprise, 2016

label: Semantic Interoperability
definition: Ability for data shared by systems to be understood at the level of fully defined domain concepts

label: Alternate Name
definition: An alternate lexical label to the preferred term for an entity.
usage_note: Alternate names are informal and unregulated by an authoritative body such as the International Mineralogical Association.

label: Authority
definition: Identifies the entity responsible for assigning and maintaining a formalized classification system

label: Classification
definition: Activity involving grouping similar or related things together; separating dissimilar or unrelated things; and arranging the resulting groups in a logical and helpful sequence

label: Classification Code
definition: Encoded classification of an object represented by a graphical symbol that conforms to an encoding scheme defined as part of the classification scheme
usage_note: Dana Number, Linnaean Taxonomy does not use a classification code, rather just a single latin term

label: Classification Level
definition: A stratified tier comprised of nodes with a shared level of granularity in a hierarchy. The distance of a level from the root is expressed as the Depth. The identifier (label) assigned to a level is referred to as the Rank.

label: Classification Name
definition: A formalized name belonging to a classification system maintained by an authoritative body.

label: Classification Rank
definition: An identifier assigned to a classification level commonly expressed using a numeric identifier or lexical label

label: Classification Scheme
definition: A method of organization according to a set of pre-established principles, usually characterized by a notation system and a hierarchical structure of relationships among the entities. Defines structure and organization of a classification including the hierarchical ranks

label: Classification System
definition: Terminological resource which has characteristics of mutual exclusiveness and exhaustiveness to aggregate data to a pre-prescribed level of specialization for a specific purpose. Extends the classification scheme concept to include the value domain used to populate a classification scheme

label: Classification Term
definition: A single concept in a classification system or scheme at any hierarchical level.

label: Classification Version
definition: A versioned instance of a classification scheme
usage_note: In a version, the categories of the classification version are split, aggregated or regrouped to provide additions or alternatives to the standard order and structure of the base version.

label: Depth
definition: The numeric distance of a nested level from the root of a hierarchy in a stratified classification scheme

label: Formal Name
definition: A name sanctioned by an authoritative body (e.g. naming authority, formal classification system) based on a defined set of unambiguous criteria and belonging to a formal nomenclature

label: Hierarchy
definition: Concept system in which all concepts are related in hierarchical relations that form a partial ordering

label: Identification
definition: Process of recognizing an entity in a particular domain as distinct from other entities.

label: Linnaean Taxonomy
definition: A classification system for grouping both living and extinct organisms governed by the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature. Generally, the parent-child relationships in the Linnaean hierarchy represent the lineage evolution between species.

label: Monohierarchy
definition: Hierarchical arrangement of concepts in a classification scheme in which each concept can have only one broader concept at the level immediately above.

label: Name
definition: Primary means of identification of objects and concepts for humans
usage_note: The term ‘Name’ refers to any label assigned to a specimen for identification, including both terms that belong to a formal classification system and informal alternate terms.

label: Naming Authority
definition: A registration authority that allocates names according to specified rules.

label: Specimen Name
definition: Refers to any name assigned to a specimen at the object level (before atomization into constituent parts). Specimen names are often written as compound terms, a concatenation of multiple informal and formal identifiers.

label: Value Set
definition: The range of values used to populate a classification scheme (or classification scheme variant)
usage_note: Equivalent to the range includes property of a classification system

label: Feature
definition: abstraction of real world phenomena
source: ISO 19101-1:2014(en) Geographic information — Reference model — Part 1: Fundamentals

label: Feature of Interest
definition: A feature of interest is an abstraction of a real-world phenomenon \which is being sampled or transformed in an act of Sampling..
usage_note: A feature of interest is defined in terms of its properties, which are qualifiable, quantifiable, observable, or operable qualities.

label: Material Sample
definition: A physical result of a sampling (or subsampling) event. Material samples are typically collected and either preserved or destructively processed.

label: Natural Geomorphological Feature
definition: A natural geomorphological feature that has been created by natural Earth processes.

label: Physiographic Feature
definition: A natural feature of the solid surface of the Earth or other planetary body.

label: Sample
definition: A feature which is intended to be representative of a `FeatureOfInterest` on which `Observations` may be made.

label: Sampling Event
definition: An activity of Sampling carries out a (Sampling) Procedure to create or transform one or more Samples.

label: Sampling Feature
definition: The feature of interest a sample is intended to be representative of.

label: Sampling Feature Type
definition: The nature of the feature such as whether the feature is the result of natural processes.

label: Sampling Location
definition: The geographic place where a sampling event takes place.

label: Biostratigraphic Unit
definition: Geologic units defined or characterized on the basis of their contained fossils. Biostratigraphic units exist only where the particular diagnostic feature or attribute on which they are based has been identified.

label: Chronostratigraphic Unit
definition: Bodies of rocks, layered or unlayered, that are defined between specified stratigraphic horizons which represent specified intervals of geologic time.

label: Geologic Unit
definition: A body of rock that persists through time, forming a discrete and definable unit. Geologic units are identified by their geometric, compositional, and internal structural characteristics, as well as their spatio-temporal relations with other rock bodies.
usage_note: Geologic Units Include both formal units (i.e. formally adopted and named in an official lexicon) and informal units (i.e. named but not promoted to the lexicon) and unnamed units (i.e. recognisable and described and delineable in the field but not otherwise formalised).

label: Geologic Unit Type
definition: A scheme that specifies concepts used to categorize types of geologic units. Unit types are differentiated based on their defining composition, temporal context, or other physical properties.

label: Law of Superposition
definition: A general law upon which all geologic chronology is based, where younger lithostratigraphic units lie atop older lithostratigraphic units
usage_note: In any sequence of layered rocks, sedimentary or extrusive volcanic, that has not been overturned, the youngest stratum is at the top and the oldest at the base; i.e., each bed is younger that the bed beneath, but older than the bed above it

label: Lithodemic Unit
definition: A defined body of predominantly intrusive, highly deformed, and (or) highly metamorphosed rock, distinguished and delimited based on rock characteristics
usage_note: Lithodemic units do not follow the law of superposition.

label: Lithology
definition: (a) The description of rocks, especially in hand specimens and outcrops, based on characteristics such as color, mineralogic composition, and grain size. (b) The physical character of a rock.

label: Lithostratigraphic Unit
definition: A defined body of sedimentary, extrusive igneous, metasedimentary, or metavolcanic strata that is distinguished and delimited based on lithic characteristics and stratigraphic position
usage_note: Lithostratigraphic units obey the law of superposition.

label: Magnetostratigraphic Unit
definition: Bodies of rock strata unified by similar magnetic characteristics which allow them to be differentiated from adjacent strata.

label: Sedimentary Facies
definition: A lithologic variant in a sedimentary unit, typically related to spatial variation in the original depositional environment or subsequent diagenetic environment.

label: Stratigraphic Column
definition: (a) A composite diagram that shows in a single column the subdivisions of part or all of geologic time or the sequence of stratigraphic units of a given locality or region (the oldest at the bottom and the youngest at the top, with dips adjusted to the horizontal) so arranged as to indicate their relations to the subdivisions of geologic time and their relative positions to each other (b) The vertical or chronologic arrangement or sequence of rock units portrayed in a geologic column.

label: Stratigraphic Unit
definition: A body of rock established as a distinct entity in the classification of the rocks, based on any of the properties or attributes or combinations thereof that rocks possess.International Stratigraphic Guide

label: Stratigraphy
definition: The description of all rock bodies forming the Earth’s crust and their organization into distinctive, useful, mappable units based on their inherent properties or attributes in order to establish their distribution and relationship in space and their succession in time, and to interpret geologic history.

label: Tectonostratigraphic Unit
definition: Geologic unit defined on basis of structural or deformation features, mutual relations, origin or historical evolution. Contained material may be igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic.
usage_note: Concept referred to as a lithotectonic unit in source

label: Indentifier
definition: Sequence of characters permanently associated with an object or aspect of an object for reference to uniquely identify it in a specified context
